newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: UNICEF pledges $15 million for Sri Lankan children.
newsitem.headline: UNICEF pledges $15 million for Sri Lankan children.

text.p: The United Nations Children's Fund (UNICEF) signed an agreement on Friday to provide 900 million rupees ($15.8 million) to Sri Lanka for improving health conditions of children, the Finance Ministry said.
The UNICEF aid for this year is to be used to combat malnutrition, provide hygiene education and prevent diseases, the ministry said in a statement.

The aid will also cover a rehabilitation programme for children caught in the country's 14-year old ethnic conflict, it said. Rebels of the minority Tamils are fighting for their separate homeland in the north and east of Sri Lanka.
Finance Secretary B.C. Perera and UNICEF representative Brita Ostberg signed the agreement on Friday, the statement said.

UNICEF has also asked foreign donor countries to extend an additional 57 million rupees ($ 10 million) for Sri Lankan children in a separate fund, to be administered by the UNICEF, the statement said.
